failures.triage_note: NOT caused by e7ece278 and NOT the activation bug - this is pre-existing and surfaced while re-running the delete flow for that commit. Raised as a failure because the runbook's Debug log protocol says to treat any new from-origin non-info line as one; the functional contract of C.member.delete-own itself passed in full (rows, child rows and files all removed). Attributed to this row because it is the flow that triggers it. The coordinator may reasonably downgrade it to an observation the way comment_count was downgraded - it corrupts nothing on THIS site because the unique index rejects the stub - but the ghost row below shows it does corrupt where no empty-slug row exists yet. Root cause: MediaRepository::set() (includes/Repository/MediaRepository.php:842-867) does an exists-check and, when the row is gone, INSERTs a stub carrying only media_id, the one key and created_at. slug is NOT NULL UNIQUE and defaults to '', so the first such stub creates a slug-less ghost row and every later one collides. Trigger: a BunnyCDN upload job completes through Action Scheduler after the member has already deleted the media, so set($id,'file_url',...) resurrects a row for an id that no longer exists. Suggested fix: make the write-back a no-op when the index row is absent, rather than inserting a stub.
failures.expected: Deleting media leaves no database error behind, and no background write-back resurrects an index row for a deleted id.
failures.actual: wp-content/debug.log: "WordPress database error Duplicate entry '' for key 'wp_mvs_media_index.slug' for query INSERT INTO wp_mvs_media_index (media_id, file_url, created_at) VALUES ('67576', 'https://mediaverse1.b-cdn.net/...', ...) made by do_action('wp_ajax_as_async_request_queue_runner') ... ActionScheduler_QueueRunner". Reproduced deterministically twice: repo->set(999777,'file_url',...) and set(999778,...) on ids absent from the index each logged the same error and created no row. Corroborating evidence that it DOES corrupt when the collision is absent: this site already carries one ghost row, media_id 63388, with an empty slug, empty title and empty media_type, created 2026-09-18 - the day before this session and not created by it.

SECTION A WAS WALKED FOR THIS STAMP on a throwaway Docker stack (WordPress 7.1.1, PHP 8.2, MariaDB 11, both 2.5.1 zips built from the clean trees), because the activation bug is only observable on a pristine database. Critically, WP_DEBUG/WP_DEBUG_LOG were OFF in that container's wp-config.php on first boot, so an empty debug.log would have proved nothing; the constants were forced on and proven with a deliberate canary notice that did land in the log before any activation was measured. A1: Free activates clean - zero debug.log output, mvs_db_version 36, 24 mvs_* tables created including mvs_media_spaces. A2: Pro activates on top clean - still zero debug.log output, 37 tables combo (24 Free + 13 Pro, matching the dev site), MVS_VERSION and MVS_PRO_VERSION both 2.5.1. A3/A4/A5 as noted below. The specific regression string, Table '...mvs_media_spaces' doesn't exist, has zero occurrences across both activations. The stack was torn down with docker compose down -v; two unrelated pre-existing docker-smoke containers on the host (up 3 and 4 days) were left untouched.

THE ACTIVATION GUARD PROVEN DIRECTLY, all three legs. Note the method takes an UNPREFIXED table name and rejects anything else via an earlier regex, so a prefixed name returns 0 without ever reaching the new code - the first attempt at this test was invalid for that reason and was redone. Leg 1, a table that does not exist ('mvs_media_spaces_notyet'): returns integer 0, wpdb->last_error empty, nothing logged. Leg 2, the exact table from the bug report ('mvs_media_spaces'): returns 0, no error. Leg 3, a real table ('mvs_media_meta') with two seeded orphan rows: returns 2, orphans remaining 0, no error - the sweep still deletes what it should.

A3/A4/A5 RESULT AND A RUNBOOK CORRECTION. On the pristine install /media/ and /my-media/ answered 200 on the first request with no manual permalink flush, and /messages/ correctly 302'd for a logged-out visitor. /compete/, /media/battles/, /media/challenges/ and /media/tournaments/ all answered 404 and mvs_page_compete was false - this is CORRECT, not a defect: competitions ship disabled by default (mvs_competitions_enabled = '0', and every mvs_pro_*_enabled toggle false), so those routes and the auto-created page are not expected until the feature is switched on. DELETE-OWN FILE REMOVAL - EVIDENCE CORRECTED. The original walk recorded this leg as passing on the basis of finding 'no e2e files on disk', which was a vacuous check because uploads are stored under hashed filenames that can never contain that marker. Re-tested properly this time by capturing the stored file_path before deleting: immediately after the 204 all six files (original, WebP sibling and two thumbnail sizes with their WebP siblings) were still present, which is BY DESIGN - MediaRepository fires mvs_media_files_orphaned and StorageCleanupService::enqueue defers the unlink to the mvs_cleanup_media_files Action Scheduler hook. Re-checked shortly afterwards: all six files gone, zero pending cleanup actions. The leg genuinely passes; the earlier evidence for it did not.

OBSERVATION, NOT A GATE FAILURE - mvs_media_index.comment_count is a read-never-written column. Filed as Basecamp card 10320950705. PRECONDITION TO ADD TO THE RUNBOOK - assert src vs build parity before a walk. Pro blocks register from MVS_PRO_DIR . 'build/blocks/' (includes/Blocks/BlockRegistrar.php:73-80), and build/ is gitignored (wpmediaverse-pro/.gitignore:23). It is refreshed only by an explicit build, so a clean git tree says nothing about what the site actually renders and the walked site can silently lag the source. That is exactly what happened: the pro-document-embed fix was correct in src/ but build/ still held the pre-fix file, so the row read as a broken fix for a whole round trip. Packaging does run grunt build -> npm run build:blocks, so the zip would have shipped the correct code - the risk is not a bad release, it is QA certifying a build the release does not contain, in either direction. Suggested check at the top of Global preconditions: for each src/blocks/*/render.php compare against build/blocks/<slug>/render.php and STOP if any differ, the same way a failing fixture cleanup is treated as a release blocker.

RUNBOOK MAINTENANCE DEBT - the runbook's own rule is that every customer-visible fix ships with a matching D row in the same PR. Five fixes verified across these runs have no D row yet: the grid query-budget batching (cache_users, one grouped COUNT, and dropping get_post_type from the typed-index privacy path), the Explore bulk-delete confirm-overlay context, the tag-autocomplete await, the pro-document-embed editor notice, and now the activation guard in delete_rows_without_media. The bulk-delete fix is partly covered by C.member.bulk-trash-restore-delete; the tag autocomplete has no runbook coverage at all on either surface. The pro-document-embed case argues for a D row that asserts the notice renders from the BUILT file, not just that the source contains it. The activation guard wants a D row that runs a migration whose cascade list names a table a later migration creates.

RE-BASELINE THE QUERY ROW - C.member.grid-render-query-budget / D.grid-render-n-plus-1 still read 'under 6 DB queries per page', which no longer describes what is being protected. After the fix the cost is a fixed per-page floor that does not grow with tile count: mvs/media-grid measured in its own cold process at perPage 1 = 12 queries, perPage 12 = 13, perPage 24 = 15, so the marginal cost is about 0.13 queries per tile (was about 2.45) and 11 extra tiles cost 1 query (was 27). Real /media/ page: 105 total queries for 12 tiles (was 117), delta against a 1-tile tag page 14 (was 25). Rewrite the row as a per-page floor (about 12-13 on this fixture) plus a marginal per-tile ceiling, since the flat curve is the real assertion. The 'byte-identical to pre-fix' claim could not be independently confirmed because the pre-fix output was not hashed during the original walk; the post-fix output has been stable at md5 864d7d596be16588198ee1cfb37aff92 across two stamps.

RUNBOOK CORRECTIONS the next editor should apply (verified against 2.5.1 code, not defects): (1) C.anon.single-media claims /p/<media_id>/ is the canonical MVS URL - it is not. /p/([0-9]+) is BuddyNext's route (buddynext/includes/Core/PageRouter.php:2358), so /p/<mvs media id>/ correctly 404s. MVS's own route is /media/<slug>/ -> mvs_media_slug, which BuddyNext redirects via the documented mvs_single_media_redirect filter; neutralising that filter for one request gives a 200 native page with h1, og:image, og:title, twitter:card, a 200 image/webp asset and 6 reaction buttons. (2) E.group-dm cites /mvs-pro/v1/groups/{id}/messages - that route does not exist; group creation is /mvs-pro/v1/groups and messaging goes through Free's /mvs/v1/conversations/{id}/messages. A non-member gets 404, not 403. (3) The Fixture cleanup block deletes mvs_reports WHERE reason LIKE 'smoke-%', but reason is an enum so that clause can never match - the marker belongs in details. (4) C.member.video-poster-fallback names PosterService::is_ffmpeg_available(), which does not exist; PosterService has only dir(), stage_bytes() and stage_client_frame(). (5) D.documents-privacy-vocabulary asserts PRIVACY_VALUES is exactly private/members/public - it is now private/space/members/public. The guarded bug is gone: nothing offers 'unlisted', and unlisted or restricted both answer 400 mvs_document_privacy_invalid. (6) C.member.lightbox-edit-modal says the Edit cog appears ONLY on /my-media/ cards - an owner also sees it in the Explore lightbox for their own media, which is not a leak (non-owner gets display:none, and PUT and DELETE answer 403). (7) C.member.bulk-trash-restore-delete describes Move to Trash plus a Trashed filter on /my-media/ - the member bulk bar offers Set privacy, Add to album, Add tags and Delete; trash lives on admin All Media. (8) A3/A4 should state that the competition routes and the /compete/ page depend on competitions being enabled, which is not the default.
